MonkMode Productivity is a cross-platform productivity app designed around the concept of monk mode — a state of deep focus, intentional habit building, and disciplined self-improvement. The app targets university students, young professionals (25–35), and the self-improvement community globally.
Give anyone the tools to live with monk-like discipline — track habits, plan their week, crush daily goals, and build unstoppable streaks — all from one beautiful, offline-first app.
Incremental — one working slice at a time
Incremental development means building one complete, shippable feature slice at a time — each piece works fully before the next begins. This is the right approach for MonkMode because:
You are a no-code developer using Cursor — focused prompts = better AI output
You have a real test user (your niece) between each slice
Each increment is something you can actually use yourself immediately
Bugs are isolated — a broken Kanban board doesn't break the habit tracker
It maps cleanly to Cursor's strength: one well-scoped task at a time

A Progressive Web App is the fastest and most user-friendly sideload option for non-technical users. No APK, no trust settings, no TestFlight.
User visits a URL (e.g. monkmode.app or a Vercel link)
iPhone: Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen → looks and behaves like a native app
Android: Chrome → Menu → Add to Home Screen → same result
Works 100% offline once installed (service worker caches all assets)
Deploy free on Vercel — your Next.js mockup is already 90% there
Set up a free Vercel account at vercel.com and connect your GitHub repo. Cursor will generate the deployment config automatically.
Android APK: Built with Expo — users download and install directly. No Play Store needed. Easy for non-technical users via clear install guide.
iOS IPA: Requires Apple Developer account ($99/yr). Users install via AltStore or Sideloadly. Provide a step-by-step install PDF.

Copy each prompt exactly into Cursor's chat. Run them in order — never skip ahead. After each prompt, test the feature on your device before moving to the next. Treat each prompt as one complete sprint.

Create a new Expo React Native project called MonkModeProductivity using Expo Router for navigation and NativeWind for styling. Set up the project with TypeScript, configure the tab navigator with 7 tabs: Home, Planner, Habits, Goals, Focus, Training, and Settings. Use a dark theme with background colour #111827 and amber accent #F59E0B. Create placeholder screens for each tab with the tab name centred on screen. Include Lucide React Native for icons.

Set up Expo SQLite and AsyncStorage in the MonkModeProductivity project. Create a database service file at /services/db.ts that initialises SQLite tables for: habits (id, name, icon, created_at), habit_completions (habit_id, date, completed), weekly_planner_slots (id, date, time, activity, category, colour), streaks (current_streak, best_streak, last_completed_date), and goals (id, title, priority, completed, type, date). Export typed functions for CRUD operations on each table.

Build the Habits screen for MonkModeProductivity. Display a list of daily habits fetched from SQLite. Each habit card shows: habit name, a progress bar showing weekly completion percentage, a checkbox (amber when checked), and an animated checkmark on completion. Add a '3/6 done' counter at the top. Include 6 default habits: Make bed, Brush teeth, Meditate, Exercise, Read 30 mins, Gratitude journal. Add a plus button to create new habits with a name and emoji icon picker. Support long-press to delete a habit with confirmation. All data persists in SQLite via the db service.

Build the Planner screen for MonkModeProductivity. Show a 7-day weekly view with Mon–Sun tab buttons at the top. Display 30-minute time slots from 5:00 AM to 11:30 PM in a scrollable list. Each slot can be empty (tappable) or filled (shows activity name + colour-coded category badge). Tapping an empty slot opens a bottom sheet modal with fields: activity name, and a category picker with 10 options each with a distinct colour: Work (blue), Personal (green), Gym (orange), Health (pink), Meal (purple), Study (yellow), Family (red), Household (grey), Pets (teal), Transport (indigo). Tapping a filled slot opens an edit/delete sheet. Show a red current-time indicator line in today's view. Save all data to SQLite.

Build the Home dashboard screen for MonkModeProductivity. Show: (1) A greeting at the top based on time of day — Good Morning/Afternoon/Evening. (2) Today's date and week number. (3) A streak card with a flame icon showing current streak number and label 'Day Streak', plus best streak below it. Streak logic: increment by 1 each day the user completes at least 1 habit. Reset to 0 if a full calendar day passes with no habits completed. Store streak in SQLite. (4) A mini habits summary card showing today's completion ratio (e.g. 3/6 habits done) with a progress bar. (5) A mini today's schedule preview showing the next 3 upcoming time blocks from the weekly planner. All data is pulled live from SQLite.
📋 PROMPT 4 — Pomodoro + Deep Work Focus Timer

Build the Focus screen for MonkModeProductivity with two timer modes. Mode 1 — Pomodoro: 25-minute work sessions, 5-minute short breaks, 15-minute long break after 4 sessions. Mode 2 — Deep Work: 90-minute focus sprint, 20-minute break. UI: a large circular countdown ring that fills with amber as time progresses, a mode toggle at the top, session counter (e.g. Session 2 of 4), and Pause/Resume/Reset buttons below. Play a soft chime sound on completion using Expo AV. Trigger vibration on completion using Expo Haptics. Timer continues running when app goes to background using Expo Task Manager. Save session history (date, mode, duration completed) to SQLite.

Build the Goals screen for MonkModeProductivity. Show three tab views: Today, This Week, This Month. Each view shows up to 5 goal cards. Each goal card has: title text, 1–5 star priority selector, completion checkbox. Completed goals show strikethrough text and move to the bottom of the list with a subtle opacity reduction. Enforce a maximum of 5 goals per view with a message 'Monk Mode: Focus on 5 or fewer' if user tries to add more. Include an add goal FAB button. Goals store in SQLite with type field (daily/weekly/monthly) and date. Add a setting toggle: 'Auto-add daily goals to Kanban board' (store preference in AsyncStorage, implement Kanban integration in Prompt 6).

Add a Kanban board view to the Planner screen in MonkModeProductivity, accessible via a toggle button next to the Weekly Planner tab. The Kanban has three columns: To Do, In Progress, Done. Each column shows a card count badge. Cards display: title and an optional colour tag. Use React Native Reanimated and React Native Gesture Handler to enable drag-and-drop between columns. Swipe left on a card to reveal a delete button with confirmation. Tap a card to expand and edit title and colour. Add a plus button on the To Do column to create new cards. If the Goals screen setting is enabled, automatically add each daily goal as a card in To Do. Store all Kanban data in SQLite.

Add journal prompts to the Home screen in MonkModeProductivity. Between 5 AM and 12 PM show a collapsible Morning card with the prompt: '3 things I am grateful for today'. Between 5 PM and midnight show a collapsible Evening card with the prompt: '3 things I achieved today'. Each card has 3 numbered text input fields. Entries save automatically to SQLite with the date. Past entries are viewable by tapping a 'View history' link that opens a modal with a scrollable date list. Add a gentle amber glow border animation to the active card to draw attention.

Implement a theme system in MonkModeProductivity. Create a ThemeContext that provides isDark boolean and toggleTheme function. Dark mode colours: background #111827, card #1F2937, text white, accent #F59E0B. Light mode colours: background #FFFBEB, card white, text #111827, accent #D97706. Apply theme colours consistently across all screens using NativeWind dynamic classes. Add a theme toggle switch in the Settings screen. Persist the user's preference in AsyncStorage. Add a smooth 300ms transition animation when switching themes.

Build the Training screen for MonkModeProductivity. Display a scrollable list of training module cards. Each card has: a thumbnail (use a coloured placeholder with an icon), a title, a short description, and a duration badge. Include 6 placeholder modules: Monk Mode Explained (15 min), The Pomodoro Method (10 min), Time Boxing Mastery (20 min), Building Atomic Habits (25 min), Deep Work Protocol (30 min), Morning Routine Blueprint (18 min). Tapping a card opens a full-screen modal that embeds a YouTube video using react-native-youtube-iframe. Use placeholder YouTube IDs for now with a note in comments to swap with real video IDs later. Add a 'Coming Soon' badge option for locked future modules.

Build the Settings screen for MonkModeProductivity with the following sections. Appearance: theme toggle (dark/light), placeholder for custom background image (show 'Coming Soon' badge). Notifications: toggle for daily habit reminder, time picker for reminder time, toggle for goal check-in reminder (all non-functional placeholders in MVP, wire up with Expo Notifications in v1.0 polish). Data: 'Reset all data' button with triple confirmation, 'Export data' button with 'Coming Soon' badge. Community: 'Accountability Partner' with 'Coming Soon' badge. AI Features: 'Smart Daily Planning' with 'Coming Soon' badge. About: app version, a quote that changes daily pulled from a local JSON array of monk mode / stoic quotes. Use a clean grouped list UI with section headers.

Add a first-launch onboarding flow to MonkModeProductivity. Use AsyncStorage to track whether onboarding has been completed. On first launch, show a 4-screen swipeable onboarding carousel before the main app. Screen 1: App name, flame icon, tagline 'Enter Monk Mode'. Screen 2: Ask 'What time do you wake up?' with a time picker — use this to set the day start time in the planner. Screen 3: 'Pick your core habits' — show the 6 default habits as toggleable chips, user selects which to activate. Screen 4: 'Set your first goal for today' — single text input. On completion save preferences to AsyncStorage and SQLite, then navigate to the Home screen. Add a skip button on every screen.

Configure MonkModeProductivity as a Progressive Web App for web deployment. Add a manifest.json with app name MonkMode Productivity, short name MonkMode, theme colour #111827, background colour #111827, display standalone, and amber app icons in 192x192 and 512x512 sizes. Configure a service worker that caches all app assets for offline use. Add a web-specific install prompt banner for browsers that support it. Configure next.config.js with PWA plugin (next-pwa). Ensure the web build produces a fully functional offline app. Add Vercel deployment configuration (vercel.json).
Set These Up Before You Start
Version control — backup all your code
Deploy your PWA — share URL with niece
Use the app yourself for 7 days before handing to your niece
Test on both iPhone and Android if possible (Expo Go app lets you do this instantly — no build needed)
Check: does data survive closing the app? Does streak count correctly?
Note anything that feels broken or confusing
Send her the Vercel URL — she adds it to her Home Screen
Ask her to use it for 2 weeks without guidance
Give her a simple feedback form (Google Forms): What did you love? What confused you? What's missing?
Watch her use it once over video call — you will see friction you never expected
Recruit 5–10 beta users from Reddit (r/productivity, r/getdisciplined, r/selfimprovement)
Offer free lifetime access in exchange for detailed feedback
Fix all critical bugs before charging money

1. One prompt = one feature. Never ask Cursor to build two features in one prompt. 2. Always test before the next prompt. A broken foundation breaks everything above it. 3. If Cursor gets confused, start a fresh chat and paste the prompt again with context. 4. Save working code to GitHub after every prompt that succeeds. 5. Use Cursor's @file and @codebase to give it context about existing code.
